subject: Private deploy performance discovery recap
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintegral.com>, Network Ops <network_ops@fintegral.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Private deploy performance discovery recap

Hi Alice / NetOps team —

Thanks for taking time earlier today. Below is a concise recap of the performance items we discussed and the proposed next steps so we can size a short private PoC for Redwood in your VPC environment. I kept items discrete so they can be handed off to your infra folks.

1) Goals & SLOs (what you asked for)
- Short interactive queries (50-300 tokens): target p95 end-to-end latency <= 120 ms (first-token within 80–120 ms)
- Long-form generation / streaming: sustain throughput of ~8–12 concurrent streams with per-token incremental latency < 40 ms
- Peak concurrency: ability to handle 200 concurrent inference sessions during business hours with graceful degradation to lower-tier model variants
- Availability target for PoC window: >= 99.5% (we will craft a test harness to measure this)

2) Network constraints you mentioned
- Primary peering via customer VPN to our on-prem appliance (VPN concentrator in us-west-2)
- Planned egress to our dedicated inference pool located in the same AZ — you expect <3 network hops, broad goal of <= 25 ms one-way internal hop latency
- VPN throughput currently provisioned at 1 Gbps; you indicated bursts up to 3 Gbps are possible with short-term bucketed capacity

3) Measurements we need from NetOps (action items for your team)
- Traceroutes from the application host(s) to the target inference IPs (both UDP and TCP) across the busiest subnets
- iperf3 tests (3x 2-minute runs) across typical window times (0800, 1300, 1800 local) to capture variance
- Representative payloads: 4 short prompts (~80 tokens), 2 mid (~300 tokens), 2 long (~1024 tokens). We will provide a small test client (script) to run these against a staging endpoint.

4) PoC sizing & timeline
- Proposed PoC duration: 72 hours of continuous testing followed by 48 hours of production-like soak (total ~5 days)
- Redwood will deploy a single model variant initially (FP16, unquantized) and provide an autoscaling sandbox with metrics and tracing hooks
- Candidate PoC window: 2028-02-06 to 2028-02-10 — provisional until you confirm maintenance windows

5) Next steps / owners
- Fintegral NetOps: run traceroute/iperf by 2028-01-17 and upload results to the shared folder (see links)
- Soojin (Redwood SE): will send test client, sample prompts, and a list of exact IPs and ports by EOD tomorrow
- Ben Carter (Redwood SE): will draft the technical acceptance criteria and sample traffic profile
- Marissa Cole (Redwood Sales): point of contact for contractual/PoC sign-off and billing holdback

Attachments: network-topology-diagram.pdf (high level), vpn-config-snippet.txt (redacted sample)

Thanks again — I think there’s a good fit here and we can scope the PoC narrowly to validate the streaming latency and max concurrent stream behavior you care about.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintegral.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Network Ops <network_ops@fintegral.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy performance discovery recap

Hi Soojin —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side and some constraints you'll need to consider:

- Our key business requirement is p95 time-to-first-token <= 150 ms for short prompts when the model is colocated in the same AZ; 120 ms is aggressive but acceptable to aim for if the network variance is low.
- VPN churn can happen during auto-rekey events; we typically see 200–400 ms microbursts — will the PoC harness detect/transparently retry?
- Our current VPN concentrator is an Azure VPN Gateway (v2 SKU) with Active-Active pair; public egress NAT sits behind the concentrator. We can open a temporary static route for the PoC.
- We will provide traceroutes and iperf results — expect them by 2028-01-16. Ops requests that you provide the IPs and exact ports so we can whitelist.

I attached the network topology diagram and a sanitized snippet of our VPN config.

On the performance numbers: we can commit to testing up to 150 concurrent streams during a PoC but not 200 unless we provision a higher throughput VPN path (we can discuss Cloud Partner peering if needed).

Thanks,

Alice Wu
VP, Platform Engineering | Fintegral
alice.wu@fintegral.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintegral.com>, Network Ops <network_ops@fintegral.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy performance discovery recap

Thanks Alice — couple of quick technical notes and an ask from the Redwood infra side so we can size the PoC correctly: 

- Microburst tolerance: Redwood's runtime will surface request retries and we can configure client-side exponential backoff. For the PoC we recommend enabling a 400 ms socket-level retry window to avoid transient aborts during IKE rekeys. We'll instrument metrics to show retry counts.
- For the streaming p95 target, we want to separate two measurements: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and per-token incremental latency. For benchmark reports please provide both.
- Action items for NetOps (detailed):
  * Run traceroute -n and mtr for 120s to our preliminary endpoint IPs (I will send the IPs in a follow-up)
  * Run iperf3 with --parallel 10 and report results (3 runs) to capture concurrency profile
  * Confirm MTU (we often see fragmentation at MTU 1400 causing ~10–20 ms variance)

If Fintegral can increase temporary VPN throughput to 2 Gbps for the PoC window we can validate up to 200 concurrent streams without introducing synthetic load on your NAT. If not, we'll scope the test to 150 concurrent streams and validate fallbacks to a smaller model variant.

I will open a HubSpot note with the proposed acceptance criteria and upload our small test client to the shared link.

—
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-01-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy performance discovery recap

Alice — thanks for the quick reply and for attaching the diagram. Two small administrative items before we lock dates: 

1) I will send a short PoC SOW and wall-of-text acceptance criteria to your procurement team by EOD today (DocuSign link will be included).
2) Can you confirm who on your side will be the NetOps point-of-contact and who has permission to approve the temporary route change? We need a name/email for the SOW.

Once we have the traceroute/iperf outputs (target 2028-01-16) we'll finalize the PoC window. Soojin / Ben — please coordinate on IPs and the test-client delivery.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Sales | Redwood Inference
